summary.text: Yuri Gagarin was a Soviet pilot and cosmonaut who became the first person to travel into outer space.
He launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome aboard Vostok 1 and completed one orbit of Earth on 12 April 1961.
He grew up in a village, worked as a foundryman at a steel plant, and became a Soviet Air Forces pilot before he was picked for the space programme.

facts.label: His flight
facts.value: Vostok 1, one orbit of Earth, 12 April 1961

facts.label: Launch site
facts.value: Baikonur Cosmodrome in the Kazakh SSR

facts.label: Early trade
facts.value: Foundryman at a steel plant in Lyubertsy

facts.label: After his flight
facts.value: Deputy training director of the Cosmonaut Training Centre

items.prompt: After his famous flight, why did Soviet officials keep Gagarin out of further spaceflights?

options.label: He failed a medical exam after his orbit
He asked to return to flying ordinary planes
They feared a national hero might be killed
His mistakes as a backup pilot had cost a life

items.explain: After his friend Komarov died in the crash of Soyuz 1, for which Gagarin was backup, officials feared a high-level national hero might be killed and banned him from further spaceflights.

items.prompt: As a boy during the German occupation, Gagarin sabotaged a soldier's work. What pushed him to do it?

options.label: The soldier tried to hang his younger brother with a scarf
The soldier burned down his school
The soldier beat his father for refusing to work
The soldier took away the family's livestock

items.explain: He became a saboteur especially after a German soldier tried to hang his younger brother Boris, and in retaliation he spoiled the soldier's battery work.

items.prompt: While studying to work with tractors in Saratov, how did Gagarin first train to fly?

options.label: At the First Chkalov Higher Air Force Pilots School
In evening classes at the steel plant
By flying a Yakovlev fighter during the war
At weekend training at a local flying club as an air cadet

items.explain: While in Saratov he volunteered at a local flying club for weekend training as a Soviet air cadet, flying a biplane and later a Yak-18.

items.prompt: Vostok 1 was Gagarin's only spaceflight. What role did he later have on Soyuz 1, the flight that killed his friend Komarov?

options.label: He commanded the mission
He served as part of the backup crew
He designed the capsule
He flew alongside it in a second capsule

items.explain: Gagarin served as the backup crew to Soyuz 1, which ended in a fatal crash.

options.label: In a MiG-15 crash while flying with an instructor
In the failed Soyuz 1 flight with Komarov
In a training accident inside a spacecraft
In a car crash on the way to the air academy

items.explain: Five weeks after being allowed to fly regular aircraft again, he died when the MiG-15 he was piloting with flight instructor Vladimir Seryogin crashed.

items.prompt: After his flight, Gagarin's work turned toward preparing others. What post did he take?

options.label: Head of all the Soviet Air Forces
Chief designer of the later Vostok capsules
Deputy training director of the Cosmonaut Training Centre
Director of the whole Baikonur Cosmodrome

items.explain: Following his spaceflight, Gagarin became the deputy training director of the Cosmonaut Training Centre, which was later named after him.
